entities.summary:
Metrology is the science of measurement: the definition, realisation, and comparison of units that make quantities mutually intelligible across laboratories, markets, and states. From ancient length and weight standards to the French metric system (1795) and today’s SI definitions anchored in physical constants, metrology underwrites trade, engineering, and experimental science.

Its modern institutional form—national metrology institutes, the Metre Convention (1875), and BIPM coordination—turns unit agreement into an international public good. Precision advances in time, mass, and electrical standards continually redefine what counts as reproducible knowledge.

Without shared metrology, industrial capitalism and global science could not scale; with it, measurement becomes a quiet infrastructure of modernity.
